svg.text: Where the cyclotomic structure of the NIST primes acts — and where it does not

g.text: P-192: p = t⁶ − t² − 1
P-224: p = t⁷ − t³ + 1
P-256: p = t⁸ − t⁷ + t⁶ + t³ − 1

svg.text: Multiplicative groups F_p*, F_{p²}* — algebraic, forced by f ± 1 in Z[t]

g.text: p + 1 = t²·Φ₁Φ₂Φ₄ = 2⁶⁴(2¹²⁸ − 1)
largest prime 46 bits — forced
p − 1: t⁶ − t² − 2 irreducible, largest 88 bits
p − 1 = t³·Φ₁Φ₂Φ₄ = 2⁹⁶(2¹²⁸ − 1)
largest prime 46 bits — forced
p + 1: t⁷ − t³ + 2 irreducible, largest 157 bits
p + 1 = t³·Φ₄·(t³ − t² + 1), largest 94 bits — forced
p − 1 = Φ₁Φ₂·(sextic): 2⁶⁴ − 1 forced, largest 160 bits
corrects “no clean factorisation” in two earlier docs
Pohlig–Hellman in F_p*: ≈ 2⁴⁴ (P-192, via p − 1), 2²³ (P-224), 2⁸⁰ (P-256). Finite-field DLP only.
In F_{p²}* the order is (p − 1)(p + 1): largest factors 88 / 157 / 160 bits.
Deployment rule it proves: never reuse these primes as DSA / Schnorr / pairing moduli.
only bridge: embedding degree ord_n(p)

svg.text: Point group E(F_p) — what it actually feels (not forced by the Solinas form)

g.text: n ∓ 1 (Cheon / Brown–Gallant, needs published [αⁱ]G)
P-192: n − 1 = 2⁴·5·2389·P83·P92 — smooth part 2¹⁷·⁵ usable
P-256: every power of two up to 2⁹⁶ has a divisor of n − 1 within 5 % — cost √(n/Q) (see cheon_cost.svg)
Frobenius cyclotomic factorisation of the points: #E(F_{p^k}) = ∏_{d|k} N(Φ_d(π))
N_d, d ≥ 3: every one keeps an unsplit cofactor of ≥ 330 bits — no small extension subgroup to address
Heights of lifts to Q (the “smaller point heights” question)
canonical lift y² = x³ − 3x + b: 0 points in 9.8·10⁶ small candidates per curve (expected 10⁻²²…10⁻³²)
lifted generator: ĥ(G̃) = 0.99·log p, ĥ/log|Δ| ≈ 1/6; two-point lift: pairing cos < 0.002, regulator ≈ ĥ(G̃)·ĥ(R̃)
a point has a lift of height ≤ H only if |x| ≤ e^H: fraction 2e^H/p of the group = the small-x factor base, nothing else
